correctness.rationale: The source theorem is specialized to coefficient spaces equal to the ambient Hilbert space, so every composition is well typed. The two displayed coefficient maps form a Parseval \(g\)-frame, the projection \(T\) has closed range and fixes every coefficient value, and \(TT^*=T\) has a one-dimensional kernel. The structural projection template and the ordinary-\(g\)-frame onto-analysis repair follow from exact operator identities.

value.rationale: The theorem claims a global operator-invertibility consequence and is presented as an extension of a valid vector-frame result. The counterexample shows that the extension fails in the smallest nontrivial dimension, even for a Parseval \(g\)-frame and \(K=I\), and isolates the precise visibility mechanism lost when vectors are replaced by operator-valued coefficients.
